citation: Randel, B., Apthorp, H., Beesley, A. D., Clark, T. F., & Wang, X. (2016). Impacts of professional development in classroom assessment on teacher and student outcomes. The Journal of Educational Research, 109(5), 491-502. https://doi.org/10.1080/00220671.2014.992581
report_number: The Journal of Educational Research, 109(5), 491-502; DOI 10.1080/00220671.2014.992581. SAME STUDY published openly as the IES/NCEE final report: Randel, B., Beesley, A. D., Apthorp, H., Clark, T. F., Wang, X., Cicchinelli, L. F., & Williams, J. M. (2011). Classroom Assessment for Student Learning: The impact on elementary school mathematics in the Central Region (NCEE 2011-4005). Washington, DC: NCEE, IES, U.S. Dept. of Education. Contract ED-06C0-0023 (REL Central / Mid-continent Research for Education and Learning).
design: Cluster (school-level) RCT; random assignment of schools blocked by district (9 block indicators). 67 Colorado elementary schools (33 intervention / 34 control) recruited from 32 districts; 409 grade 4-5 mathematics teachers (178 intervention, 231 control). Intervention = Classroom Assessment for Student Learning (CASL) self-administered teacher PD in formative/classroom assessment (textbook + DVDs + learning teams; ~1 training year + 1 implementation year, ~31 hrs actual vs 60 recommended). Comparison = business-as-usual PD. Outcome = student mathematics scale scores on the statewide Colorado Student Assessment Program (CSAP), grades 4 & 5, spring 2009 (end of implementation year). Final student impact sample = 9,596 (4,420 intervention, 5,176 control). Impacts estimated with a 2-level mixed model (students within schools, block fixed effects), pretest-adjusted (student- and cluster-mean CSAP pretest), so clustering is accounted for.
problems: LEGAL-OA SOURCING: The assigned label 'Randel et al. 2016' refers to the journal article in The Journal of Educational Research (DOI 10.1080/00220671.2014.992581), which is CLOSED/paywalled at Taylor & Francis (Unpaywall oa_status='closed', no oa_locations; OpenAlex is_oa=false; ERIC EJ1105445 provides no full text; publisher page returns HTTP 403). NO legal OA copy of the journal version exists. HOWEVER, the 2016 journal article reports the SAME randomized controlled trial (same authors, same CASL intervention, same 67 Colorado schools, same 9,596 students, same grade 4-5 statewide-math outcome, same null finding) as the IES/NCEE final report NCEE 2011-4005 (ERIC ED517969), which is in the PUBLIC DOMAIN and openly hosted at files.eric.ed.gov. Numbers were extracted from that legal open NCEE report (data/fulltext/randel_2016.pdf). No piracy site was used. The journal article and the NCEE report are the same study; the impact estimate (0.58 scale points, SE 3.47) is identical. | SUBJECT SCOPE: This study examined MATHEMATICS ONLY. Both the journal article (abstract: 'failed to yield statistically significant impacts of CASL on student mathematics achievement') and the NCEE report confirm a single primary student-achievement outcome (CSAP math). There is NO reading/literacy student-achievement contrast in this study, despite the synthetic FIXTURE file listing a 'Reading' row for row_id 94 (that fixture is explicitly SYNTHETIC, not real data). Only STEM (math) effect sizes are extracted. | GRADE BAND: The registry codes grades '3-6', but the actual study covers grades 4 and 5 only (grade 3 CSAP was used as the pretest covariate, grade 6 not involved). grade_band recorded as '4-5'. | STANDARDIZER / g METHOD: g computed per spec as d = b/s with b = the model-based HLM impact coefficient (0.58 CSAP scale points) and s = the pooled raw posttest SD from Appendix J Table J1 (sqrt of pooled intervention SD 78.21 (n=4,420) & control SD 80.77 (n=5,176) = 79.60). The report's own effect size (Glass's d = 0.01, Table 4.1) instead used the CONTROL-group SD derived from null-model variance components (Appendix G); using the control raw SD (80.77) gives b/SD=0.0072, essentially identical to our pooled-SD g=0.007 and to the report's rounded 0.01. Variance of g taken from the impact SE: SE(d)=impact_se/s, Var(g)=J^2*SE(d)^2. | CLUSTERING/ICC: impacts are already cluster-adjusted (2-level HLM), so cluster_adjusted=true. ICC = 0.16 (unconditional null model, Appendix I; reported text gives between-school var 1,003.23 / total 6,202.69 = .16; note Table I1's row labels are transposed relative to the prose, but the ICC of .16 is unambiguous). | COHORT/GRADE EXPLORATORY analyses (Cohort 1 = grade 5, two years of CASL exposure; Cohort 3 = grade 4, one year of exposure) are confounded with exposure duration, are explicitly labelled exploratory, and are recorded here as secondary/subgroup rows (not the headline contrast).

effect_sizes.arm_label: CASL classroom-assessment PD (full sample, grades 4 & 5 combined)
effect_sizes.test_name: Colorado Student Assessment Program (CSAP), mathematics scale score
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (spring 2009 CSAP, end of CASL implementation year)
effect_sizes.g_method: d = b/s where b = HLM benchmark impact coefficient (Intervention) = 0.58 CSAP scale points (Table K3 / Table 4.1 'Adjusted posttest', pretest-adjusted 2-level mixed model with block fixed effects) and s = pooled raw posttest SD = 79.60 (Appendix J Table J1: intervention SD 78.21 n=4,420, control SD 80.77 n=5,176). g = J*d, J=1-3/(4*df-1) with df=N-2=9,594 -> J~=1.000. Var(g)=J^2*(impact_se/s)^2, impact_se=3.47. (Report's own Glass d using control SD = 0.01, Table 4.1; matches.)
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 4.1 p.67; Table K3 p.131; Appendix J Table J1 p.129; Appendix I Table I1 p.127; Exec summary p.7
effect_sizes.notes: Headline confirmatory outcome (the study's single primary student outcome). Intervention adjusted mean 502.49 (SE 2.53) vs control 501.91 (SE 2.44); estimated difference 0.58, p=.87 (not statistically significant). Study powered to detect 0.25 SD. All 67 schools analyzed as randomized (intent-to-treat); missing data multiply imputed (40 datasets). ICC=0.16 from unconditional model (between-school var 1,003.23 / total 6,202.69). Math-only study; immediate end-of-implementation-year wave (spring 2009).
